cases.scenario: Fresh database migrates to schema v1 and missing-profile reads return safe defaults.
cases.boundary: No profile row exists; result limit defaults to 10 and recency persistence defaults on.
cases.ownership: Database application_id and owner_id belong to InfoBoard.

cases.scenario: Normal profile configuration and activation metadata remain isolated by profile_id.
cases.boundary: Read for profile B returns its own defaults, not profile A values.
cases.ownership: Only the requested profile's rows are visible or resettable.

cases.scenario: Initial migration is transactional and idempotent across reopen.
cases.boundary: Repeated migration does not duplicate history or change schema version.
cases.ownership: Migration history and application_id remain InfoBoard-owned.

cases.scenario: A failed migration rolls back DDL, migration history, and user_version.
cases.boundary: Failure occurs after one valid DDL statement in the same migration transaction.
cases.ownership: The previous supported schema remains reopenable.

cases.scenario: A future schema version is reported without modifying its database file.
cases.boundary: On-disk user_version exceeds the running host's supported version.

cases.scenario: Corrupt SQLite bytes are quarantined and a fresh schema is rebuilt.
cases.boundary: Original bytes and owner marker survive in the timestamped quarantine directory.
cases.ownership: Only the reserved InfoBoard database and sidecars move; quarantine is retained.

cases.scenario: Activation retention removes records older than 30 days and keeps at most 500 per profile.
cases.boundary: An activation exactly at the 30-day cutoff is retained; ties use activation_id order.
cases.ownership: Profile A pruning does not consume or delete profile B rows.

cases.scenario: Diagnostics retention removes records older than 7 days and limits logical payload to 10 MiB.
cases.boundary: UTF-8 payload_bytes counts encoded bytes; the oldest diagnostic is pruned first.
cases.ownership: Only redacted diagnostic payload bytes contribute to the cap.

cases.scenario: Unavailable persistence returns defaults and does not expose database error text.
cases.boundary: Repository has no database handle; query and activation runtime state remain independent.
cases.ownership: No memory database or substitute persistence is created.

cases.scenario: Profile reset, full reset, and uninstall are idempotent and preserve unrelated artifacts.
cases.boundary: Global diagnostics survive profile reset; browser-state and unowned file sentinels survive uninstall.
cases.ownership: Only InfoBoard rows, its fixed database/sidecars, and marker-owned quarantine directories are removed.
